title: Light
seo_title: Year 7 Science: Light Worksheets (Reflection, Refraction, Colour)
standard_text: The similarities and differences between light waves and waves in matter; light waves travelling through a vacuum; speed of light; the transmission of light through materials: absorption, diffuse scattering and specular reflection at a surface; use of ray model to explain imaging in mirrors, the pinhole camera, the refraction of light and action of convex lens in focusing (qualitative); the human eye; colours and the different frequencies of light, white light and prisms (qualitative only); differential colour effects in absorption and diffuse reflection.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 science worksheets on light: the speed of light, reflection and the law of reflection, refraction, the spectrum, coloured filters and coloured objects. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Angle of incidence = angle of reflection. Objects reflect their own colour.
body_html:
How to think about it

Light travels in straight lines at 300,000 km/s, even through a vacuum.

  • Reflection: angle of incidence = angle of reflection, measured from the normal.
  • Refraction: light bends when it goes into a different material (towards the normal into glass).
  • White light is a mix of colours. Filters let their own colour through; objects reflect their own colour.
Example

Angle of incidence 35°. Angle of reflection?

They are equal

Answer: 35°

Example

A blue ball in red light?

No blue light to reflect

Answer: black

Common mistakes

  • Measuring angles from the mirror instead of the normal.
  • Thinking a red filter adds red to light.
  • Thinking a blue object looks blue in red light.

faq.q: What is the law of reflection?
faq.a: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. Both angles are measured from the normal, a line at 90° to the mirror.
Light bending as it passes from one material into another, because its speed changes. Going from air into glass, it bends towards the normal.

faq.q: Why do objects look different colours in coloured light?
faq.a: An object reflects only its own colour of light. If that colour is not in the light shining on it, it absorbs everything and looks black.
